findings.claim: The process-wide translation cache in I18n.translate (translate_accelerator.rb) is keyed only on the key, the locale and the backend object id. It does not include SiteSetting.default_locale or the site, even though FallbackLocaleList#[] puts the default locale in the fallback chain. As a result, stale fallback strings stay cached after an admin changes default_locale, and in multisite one site's fallback text is served to another site.

In ensure_loaded!, the lazy initialization `@loaded_locales ||= []` is not protected by LOAD_MUTEX. Concurrent threads read and write @loaded_locales without synchronization, which can cause lost writes or double loading.
The '# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb' comment implies an ordering directive, but nothing reads it; load order is purely the alphabetical sort of file names.
SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym is called without a nil guard, so it raises NoMethodError if default_locale is nil.
The PR adds no tests for the new i18n fallback system, including FallbackLocaleList#[], FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!, I18n.ensure_loaded!, the fallback order, and fallback/cache interaction.

Locales are not normalized to one type (Symbol or String) before the @loaded_locales include? check and insertion. Because :en != 'en', the same locale passed as a String and as a Symbol produces duplicate entries and redundant loads.

The new public I18n.ensure_loaded! duplicates load_locale's existing already-loaded guard. Its `@loaded_locales ||= []` is also inconsistent with translate, which dereferences @loaded_locales without a guard.
I18n::Backend::Pluralization is included via send(:include, ...) even though include is public since Ruby 2.1.
I18n::Backend::Fallbacks is included via send(:include, ...) even though include is public since Ruby 2.1.

I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! is called only in ApplicationController#set_locale. Non-request paths (Sidekiq jobs, mailers, I18n.with_locale callers, rake tasks, console) therefore never load the fallback locales, so lookups yield 'translation missing' and the LRU cache stores that result.

Fallbacks are now enabled in all environments, including development and test, instead of only production/profile/cloud66. This hides missing translations behind English text and can break specs that expect missing-translation output.
Backend classes are monkey-patched via send(:include), which is fragile across gem upgrades.

FallbackLocaleList inherits from Hash but only implements [] and ensure_loaded!. Because the underlying Hash storage is never populated, other Hash methods (fetch, keys, each, to_h) return empty results or raise.
ensure_loaded! is called on every request in set_locale.
The custom fallback list drops the standard locale-ancestor fallbacks, so regional locales skip the matching base-language translations.
